observations.seen: The Paris clay frame has a warm low key light with a brighter pool at center court and reads well. The Dubai frame is almost uniformly lit beige with very little value separation between floor, stands and sky. The Moon frame drops everything outside the court into near-black.

Players, net, umpire chair and stand boxes cast directional shadows, and the long net and player shadows on the Paris clay are the strongest moment. Shadows are hard-edged with no contact darkening under feet or crowd figures, and in the close blue-court frame the player shadows are small dark blobs.
Every surface is matte. The court, the player helmets on the Moon and the poles show no environment reflection or specular response.

Each venue is the same layout on an infinite flat ground plane with stands set as boxes. The same lattice tower prop appears behind both Paris and Dubai, and the Moon venue is a black void with a sphere moon. Floodlight poles stand alone with no visible light fixtures.
No indoor haze, light shafts or depth fog is visible. The only depth cue is the blurred tower and sky band at the top of the Paris and Dubai frames.

Flat vertex-color shading throughout. The blue court has a faint diagonal surface texture in the close frame, but clay, sand and hard court otherwise read as single flat colors with no wear or line paint variation.

The crowd is repeated low-poly capsule figures in two rows per stand with identical poses. The umpire chair and bench are plain boxes. The players are simple but readable, with racket and cap silhouettes.

In three frames the court sits centered at roughly 30–35% of the frame, which matches the target. Large empty floor margins fill the lower corners. The close blue-court frame fills more of the screen and crops the stands.

A consistent high broadcast angle looks down the court from behind the near baseline. It uses a perspective camera rather than the orthographic one the recipe expects, and the stands converge noticeably.
There is mild vignetting in the close blue-court frame. The Dubai frame looks washed out, with no contrast curve, bloom or color grading to separate the court from the surround.

The score is world-space text on the back stand wall ('PARIS 0-0 0-0') with no player names or serve indicator. The far player occludes the 'AURA SLAM' board. Gameplay feedback is limited to a pale yellow service box highlight and a pink or red target ring.
